issues.finding: The formal definition permits an empty sphere, so the assertion that the center singleton is the innermost sphere needs a nonempty qualification. Its strict closeness comparison must also concern other worlds, rather than the center itself present in larger spheres.
issues.proposed_resolution: Call the center singleton the innermost nonempty sphere and compare the center with other worlds; retain every formal model hypothesis.

issues.location: inheritance of non-vacuous satisfaction by contained spheres, source lines 102–103
issues.finding: An inner sphere need not contain an antecedent world, so the entire non-vacuous clause does not hold at every contained sphere. The final innermost-sphere conclusion also assumes existence despite the next paragraph denying that assumption.
issues.proposed_resolution: Restrict inheritance to contained antecedent-admitting spheres and condition the innermost antecedent-admitting conclusion on existence.

issues.location: infinite descending antecedent-admitting chain, source lines 107–112
issues.finding: An infinite descending chain alone does not imply that no smallest antecedent-admitting sphere exists; such a sphere could lie below the whole chain.
issues.proposed_resolution: Specify the example's intersection as only the center world, where the antecedent is false. Any putative smallest antecedent-admitting sphere would lie in that intersection, yielding the required contradiction.

translation_treatment: Translated model definitions, satisfaction clauses, diagram explanation and limit discussion; corrected only the audited prose scopes and example condition. Formal formulas, model hypotheses, legacy file identity and all diagram geometry remain unchanged.
